title: Prioritize local semantic honesty; bridge mismatch with explicit docs
context: helm.ts's fields named *Byte were actually UTF-16 code unit indices (JS char offsets), not UTF-8 bytes. The misleading names could confuse future readers about what the values represent. The shared ParsedSymbol/ParsedCall types also have *Byte fields that are semantically char offsets in practice (issue #84), but changing those would ripple across all callers.
decision: Rename helm.ts's fields to *Char to reflect their actual semantics. When merging into the shared ParsedSymbol/ParsedCall array in indexer.ts, map the *Char values into the array's *Byte fields with explicit documentation explaining that both are char offsets in practice—preserving the shared interface while fixing local correctness and surfacing the broader semantic bug.
consequences: helm.ts is now locally semantically correct and self-documenting
An impedance mismatch is created at the merge point in indexer.ts that requires ongoing documentation
The bug in the shared types (ParsedSymbol/ParsedCall naming *Byte for char offsets) is now explicitly documented but unfixed
Future refactor to fix the shared types is clearly identified as issue #84
helm.ts and indexer.ts now both carry detailed comments about the semantic mismatch
alternatives_rejected: Rename *Byte to *Char throughout ParsedSymbol/ParsedCall to truly fix the root issue (large refactor affecting all callers, deferred to issue #84)
Keep helm.ts's misleading *Byte names to avoid a merge-point mismatch (perpetuates the lie locally)
Add a conversion layer that translates char offsets to actual UTF-8 byte offsets (wasteful, incorrect for the actual use case)
